key_thresholds.hap_major_source: 10 tpy single HAP or 25 tpy aggregate HAP PTE
key_thresholds.regulated_air_pollutant_major_source: 100 tpy PTE unless lower nonattainment thresholds apply

existing permits or enforceable PTE limits

summary: Under 40 CFR part 70, approved state/local Title V programs must permit “Any major source” and other listed source categories. A “major source” includes a source with potential to emit 10 tpy or more of any listed HAP or 25 tpy aggregate HAPs, or 100 tpy or more of any air pollutant subject to regulation; lower major-source thresholds apply in specified nonattainment areas (e.g., ozone VOC/NOx thresholds of 100/50/25/10 tpy by classification). EPA’s definition of potential to emit is the maximum capacity considering only federally enforceable physical/operational limits. California air districts implement Title V programs, but the facility county/jurisdiction is unknown, so the controlling air district and any local/nonattainment thresholds cannot be resolved. Based only on the project description—storing 60 gallons of solvent at a coating shop with a coating/paint operation—there is no evidence that facility-wide PTE reaches 100 tpy regulated pollutants or 10/25 tpy HAP thresholds, and no evidence it is an affected acid-rain source, solid waste incinerator, or EPA-designated category. Therefore Title V applicability is indeterminate pending facility location, solvent composition/HAP content, VOC content, annual throughput/usage, coating booth emissions/PTE, controls and enforceable limits, and current permits; on the limited facts, a Title V permit is not triggered by the stated 60-gallon storage alone.
title: H-AIR-TITLE-V — Title V operating permit applicability cannot be confirmed without location/PTE, but 60 gal solvent storage at a coating shop is not itself enough to indicate a major source
